## Astra Chemistry — A hidden failure in the previous construction

The previous locally reanchoring NCL relay has an important inconsistency.

It assumes that product-attached PNA handles maintain a local growth frontier, but its cleanup procedure also calls for denaturing the PNA–DNA hybrids to remove unreacted donors.

A fully denaturing wash removes the DNA-bound state of both free donors and product-attached handles. Covalent attachment preserves the product's handles, but does not preserve their positions on the template.

Consequently, the earlier constant-reaction-rate model is justified only after demonstrating that the product can regain its correct local register sufficiently quickly. Covalent retention alone is insufficient.

The distinction suggests a better operation: remove untethered donors through dissociation and physical escape, while allowing product-attached handles to dissociate and rapidly rebind locally. The two populations can have identical recognition sequences; their different covalent topology creates the potential separation mechanism.

This does not require a new bond sensor, but it does require a quantitatively adequate difference between free-donor escape and rooted-handle recovery.

### 1. Exact recovery mechanism: a small rolling set of anchors

I modeled the most recent \\(m\\) product-attached PNA handles as reversible molecular anchors. Each docked handle detaches at rate \\(u\\); each detached handle can rebind at rate \\(v\\), provided at least one other local anchor remains correctly registered.

Losing the final anchor destroys the fast local register, though the chemically intact peptide may still recover by slower rehybridization from the root.

In parallel, an unreacted donor can detach from DNA and escape into the flowing wash solution. Unlike the product-attached handle, an escaped donor has no covalent path back to its original rooted molecule.

The resulting finite-state model gives the probability of maintaining local registration throughout cleanup, followed by restoration of the complete local anchor set.

Illustrative 1,024-cycle relay, 10 bound donor molecules to clear per cycle

Assumed rates: PNA detachment 0.03 s⁻¹ for both product and donor; local product rebinding 1 s⁻¹; free-donor rebinding 0.03 s⁻¹; physical donor escape 1 s⁻¹. No irreversible product aging in this comparison.

TOPOLOGICAL INVARIANT AND PROOF
Assume (i) rooted product remains linked to support throughout chemistry and
wash, (ii) only a correct amide can add a new rooted donor tag that survives
S-acyl challenge, (iii) all unrooted donor tags are removed before next fuel,
(iv) incorporated tags re-register at their own codons, (v) old-site binding
and downstream misbinding do not cause stable incorrect chemistry, and
(vi) reactive successor protection prevents two additions per macrocycle.
Let X_j be the rooted product carrying exactly a correctly ligated prefix of j
modules with tags 1..j. An unsuccessful reversible reaction restores X_j.
A correct ligation produces X_{j+1}. Thus, under these stated assumptions,
X_j -> X_j or X_{j+1} per cycle, and two X_j with different j can proceed
independently. Exhaustive finite-history tests in
astra_chemistry_vacancy_frontier.py check the state-machine invariant. The
assumptions are precisely the critical *physical* missing operations; abstract
prefix induction does not establish them. Wrong stable amides may add tag j and
falsely update the prefix. Covalent thioester intermediates survive denaturing
if chemical cleanup has not resolved them.

ROOTED PREFIX IS A CONDITIONAL STATE MACHINE
The1624 source explicitly assumes stable rooted cargo, complete removal of unrooted donors, resolved transient S-acyl connections, correct positional re-registration, suppression of old/future wrong stable chemistry and reactive successor protection. Only then does induction give prefixj ->j orj+1, including independently stalled lineages. A temporary thioester and a stable amide can both keep a tag covalently root-connected: topology alone does not distinguish productive completion. A wrong stable amide also survives this selector. No bond sensor or successful chemical integration is supplied by the prefix induction.
The later1717 correction is substantive and remains CURRENT: full denaturation destroys the docked position of product-attached as well as free handles. Covalent retention preserves handles, not register. The1624 constant local-rate comparison is conditional on reacquiring that register quickly and correctly. Its native prose must not silently imply that a denaturing wash preserves local position. Mild wash/kinetic recapture is a proposed different physical interface, not a demonstrated repair.
Existing accepted U1016-multivalent-clearance was reopened through its actual proof37–49, not merely its title. Its independent-arm chain has n->n-1 atnu,n->n+1 at(m-n)a and an absorbing physical wash sink0 for the nuisance island. The1717 recent-product-anchor model has the same possible birth/death algebra while0 means loss of FAST LOCAL REGISTER of a retained correct product, with slower root-mediated recovery outside that target. Slow first hitting0 harms nuisance clearance but can protect correct registration. Therefore identical generator vocabulary cannot justify transferring the reward/observation role or calling product rebinding a clearance failure. Its old first-passage expectation does not itself supply a complete finite-time joint donor-clearance/registry kernel. Old U1020's no-rebinding/register-loss budget and U1016's explicit sink assumptions remain valid; no old scientific acceptance is withdrawn.
